newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-CHANG CRASHES OUT AT QUEEN'S, SAMPRAS POWERS ON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHANG CRASHES OUT AT QUEEN'S, SAMPRAS POWERS ON.

text.p: World number two Michael Chang crashed out of the Queen's grasscourt tournament on Wednesday falling in three sets to Australia's Scott Draper.
The American looked uncomfortable on the west London grass, falling on his fifth match point 6-3 2-6 7-6.
In contrast, world number one Pete Sampras strode confidently into the third round with a straight sets win over Argentina's Javier Frana.
Chang failed to come to grips with Draper's sharp attacking game, the left-hander using angles and touch-play to outsmart the second seed and take the opening set 6-3.
But in the second set Chang began to find his range and drilled shots past the Australian, winning the set 6-2 and appeared on the way to victory after racing to a 4-2 lead in the final set.
Draper counter-attacked by charging the net, breaking the American's rhythm and had four match points with Chang serving at 4-5.
Chang himself had a match point in the tie break at 6-5 up but missed his chance and on Draper's fifth opportunity to tie up matters, Chang ballooned a forehand long to hand him victory.
Sampras, looking happy to be back on grass after his third round exit at the French Open, made light work of Frana on an overcast day, advancing 6-3 6-2.
"It was like I never left...I played good out there," said Sampras, winner of the London tournament in 1995.
Sampras, who crashed out to Swede Magnus Norman in Paris while suffering from an upset stomach, was back to his imperious best on the fast grass surface.
The American broke his opponent in the fourth game with a deftly sliced backhand return to move 3-1 ahead.
A lapse of concentration allowed Frana to immediately break back but that seemed to wake up the American and he won the last three games to take the first set.
Frana held serve in the first game of the second set but Sampras then reeled off five games in a row and a subtle drop volley on his second match point at 5-2 was all he needed to secure victory.
"It's always a bit difficult your first grasscourt match after a month-and-a-half on clay but I've got no complaints about the way I played out there," he said.
"I feel fine physically and was pretty solid out there."
Third seed Goran Ivanisevic overcame a slow start to beat India's Leander Paes 7-6 6-3 in another second round match.
